tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

Hidden files (dotfiles such as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or `.eslintrc.json`) are searched by default. To also search files excluded by `.gitignore` (such as `node_modules` or build outputs), set `include_ignored` to `true`. Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always skipped for safety, even when `include_ignored` is `true`.

path.description: File or directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Omit to search the current working directory. Use Read instead when you already know a concrete file path and need its contents.

glob.description: Optional glob filter for which files to search, e.g. `*.ts`. Matched against each file's full absolute path, so a path-anchored pattern like `src/**/*.ts` silently matches nothing — use a basename pattern (`*.ts`), or anchor with `**/` (`**/src/**/*.ts`). To scope the search to a directory, use `path` instead.

type.description: Optional ripgrep file type filter, such as ts or py. Prefer this over `glob` when filtering by language or file kind: it is more efficient and less error-prone than an equivalent glob pattern.

output_mode.description: Shape of the result. `content` shows matching lines (honors `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-n`, and `head_limit`); `files_with_matches` shows only the paths of files that contain a match, most-recently-modified first (honors `head_limit`); `count_matches` shows per-file match counts as `path:count` lines, preceded by an aggregate total line. -i.description: Perform a case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

-n.description: Prefix each matching line with its line number. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`. Defaults to true.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`; takes precedence over `-A` and `-B`.

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries after offset. Defaults to 250. Pass 0 for unlimited.

offset.description: Number of leading lines/entries to skip before applying `head_limit`. Use it together with `head_limit` to page through large result sets. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline matching, where the pattern can span line boundaries and `.` also matches newlines. Defaults to false.

include_ignored.description: Also search files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). All hypotheses confirmed. Here is the full report.

# Probe Results (scope: validity rules & edge inputs)

Output format below: `scheme | authority | port | path | query | fragment | is_valid`, with `∅` = empty/blank line. All runs exit 0 (exit 1 only when argv missing).

## Empty / whitespace / trivial inputs
- `""` → `∅ | ∅ | -1 | ∅ | ∅ | ∅ | 0` — **only all-empty input that is invalid on its own**
- `" "` → path=` `, valid=**1**; `"   "` → path=`   `, valid=**1**
- `$'\t'` → path=tab, valid=**1**; `$'\n'` → path=newline, valid=**1**; `$'\r'` → path=CR, valid=**1**; `$' \n '` → valid=**1**
- `"a"`, `"x"`, `"."`, `".."`, `":"`, `"/"`, `"@"` → all go to path verbatim, valid=**1**
- `"?"` → all blank, valid=**0**; `"#"` → valid=**0**; `"?#"` → valid=**0**
- `"?queryonly"` → query=`queryonly`, valid=**0**; `"#fragonly"` → fragment=`fragonly`, valid=**0**; `"?q#f"` → query+fragment set, valid=**0** (query/fragment alone never make it valid)

## Scheme-only / authority-only / path-only
- `"http"`, `"http:"`, `"http:/"`, `"http:x"`, `"http:/x"`, `"mailto:foo@bar.com"`, `"a:b"` → **no scheme parsed** (scheme requires literal `://`); whole string is path, valid=**1**
- `"http://"` → scheme=http, rest blank, valid=**0**; `"x://"` → valid=**0**; `"://"` → valid=**0**; `"://x"` → scheme ∅, authority=x, valid=**1**
- `"http:///"` → authority ∅, path=`/`, valid=**1**; `"http://?q"` / `"http://#f"` / `"a://?q"` → valid=**0**
- `"//example.com"`, `"/path/only"`, `"path/only"`, `"example.com"` → path, valid=**1**

## The host-empty discovery (refines the validity rule)
- `"http://:80"` → scheme=http, authority=`:80`, port=80, valid=**0** (!)
- `"http://:abc"` / `"http://:"` / `"http://:65536"` → authority ∅, port -1, valid=**0**
- `"http://:80/p"` → valid=**1** (path saves it); `"http://:80#f"` → valid=**0**
- `"http://user@"` → authority=`user@`, valid=**0**; `"http://user@/p"` → valid=**1**
- `"http://@"` → authority ∅, valid=**0**; `"http://@host"` → authority=`host`, valid=**1**
- ⇒ **is_valid = (host non-empty) OR (path non-empty)**. Authority string alone isn't the criterion — `:80` has non-empty authority but empty host → invalid. Query/fragment/scheme never contribute.

## Spaces, control chars, non-ASCII
- `"foo bar"`, `" http://example.com"` (scheme=` http`!), `"http://example.com "`, `"http://exa mple.com"`, `"http://a b/p?q#f"` → all valid=**1**, spaces preserved verbatim everywhere, never trimmed
- Tab/CR/newline/\x01/\x7F inside input → preserved verbatim in path, valid=**1**
- `"héllo://wörld.com/päth"` → scheme/authority/path keep raw UTF-8 bytes, valid=**1**
- Invalid UTF-8 (`\xc3\x28...`) → passed through raw, valid=**1**. No encoding validation at all.

## Very long strings
- 10,000-char path-only string → path len=10000, valid=**1**; `http://h/` + 5000×`p` → path len=5001, valid=**1**. No length limit observed.

## Delimiter precedence & repeated delimiters
- `"a?b://c"` → path=a, query=`b://c` (no scheme!) — `?` is split **before** `://` is searched
- `"a#b://c"` → path=a, fragment=`b://c`; `"http://a/b#c?d"` → fragment=`c?d` — `#` split first of all
- `"http://a/b?c/d#e"` → path=/b, query=`c/d`, fragment=e. Order: `#`, then `?`, then `://`, then `/`
- `"a??b"` → query=`?b`; `"a##b"` → fragment=`#b`; `"a#?b"` → fragment=`?b`; `"a?#"` → query ∅, fragment ∅, valid=1 (path=a)
- `"a://b://c"` → scheme=a, authority=b, path=`//c`; `"http://a//b///c"` → path=`//b///c` (repeated `/` kept)
- `"a/b://c"` → scheme=`a/b` (!), authority=c; `"a b://c"` → scheme=`a b`. Scheme = literally anything before first `://` (no charset check: digits, `+ - . _`, spaces, tab, newline all accepted — `"ht\ttp://x"` → scheme=`ht\ttp`)
- `"HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM"` → scheme lowercased to `http`; authority/path NOT lowercased
- `"http://exa?mple.com"` → authority=`exa`, query=`mple.com`; `"http://exa#mple.com"` → authority=`exa`, fragment=`mple.com` (`?`/`#` terminate authority)

## `@` and `:` inside authority (mechanism behind validity)
- Authority is split at **first `@`** into userinfo/hostport; printed authority = `userinfo@host[:port]`, but when userinfo is empty the bare `@` vanishes: `"@host"`→`host`, `"@@host"`→`@host`, `"user@"`→`user@`, `"a@b@c"`→`a@b@c` (reconstruction)
- Host/port split at **first `:`** in hostport. Port parsed strtol-style: skips leading spaces, accepts `+`, stops at first non-digit; valid only in 0–65535, else port=-1
- Printed authority is **reconstructed** as `host:` + decimal port when port parses: `"host:00080"`→`host:80`, `"host:+80"`→`host:80`, `"host: 80"`→`host:80`, `"host:12x34"`→`host:12` (port 12), `"host:80:90"`→`host:80` (port 80), `"host:abc"`→`host` (port -1, `:abc` dropped), `"host:"`→`host`, `"host:65535"`→ok, `"host:65536"`/`"host:99999"`/`"host:-1"`→port -1, port part dropped
- `"http://user:pass@host.com:8080/p?q#f"` → authority=`user:pass@host.com:8080`, port=8080, valid=1

# Inferred rules for my scope

1. **is_valid = (!host.empty() || !path.empty())**, where host = authority after stripping userinfo (at first `@`) and port (at first `:`). Nothing else matters: scheme, query, fragment, whitespace, control chars, non-ASCII bytes are all irrelevant to validity.
2. Consequently the minimal invalid inputs are: `""`, and any input whose path and host both end up empty: `?`, `#`, `?q`, `#f`, `?q#f`, `://`, `x://`, `http://?q`, `http://@`, `http://user@`, `http://:80`, `http://:abc`, `http://:65536`.
3. A single space, tab, newline, control char, or even `.`/`:`/`/`/`@` as the whole input is **valid** (it lands in path). There is no whitespace trimming, no control-char rejection, no UTF-8 validation, no length cap (tested to 10k).
4. Parsing order: split `#` (fragment) → split `?` (query) → find first `://` (scheme = anything before it, lowercased, no charset rules) → authority up to next `/`, rest is path.
5. Port (tangent to validity, since it determines host): first `:` in hostport, strtol-like parse, must be 0–65535 else -1; authority output is reconstructed from parse results, so a garbage/invalid/oversized port silently vanishes from authority (and can thereby flip is_valid to 0, e.g. `http://:65536`).
